analysis: Reviewed scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (base text units; the head diff is only a truncated patch excerpt). The change is a CI test script for the Darkbloom runner-route step. It introduces run_labels(), LINUX_BASE/MACOS_BASE, sized() returning run-scoped labels, and new tests (head lines ~422-472) asserting that the request carries an X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 header and that only current-run labels are accepted. The visible patch tightens the router contract: a grant must match the run-scoped label array exactly, so an older run's labels cannot be reused. The test file has no production runtime path: no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or billing logic. The canonical threat model (provider/native runtime: T-041 etc.) does not cover CI routing, and nothing here touches A-001..A-020 or TB-002..TB-014. The tests still pin that UNROUTED release and credentialed workflows keep literal blacksmith runners, so release signing is not routed to the self-hosted plane. Limitation: the patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so the later head tests, and the actual darkbloom-route.yml change that implements the run-scoped label validation, were not visible in this batch. The integration pass should confirm the workflow change enforces the same exact-match logic and does not weaken the fallback behavior. No concrete security regression was identified in the supplied lines.
